short: Effects of combined surface treatments of aluminium nanopart
title: Effects of combined surface treatments of aluminium nanoparticle on its corrosion resistance before and after inclusion into an epoxy coating

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Epoxy coatings on steel need both a barrier and an active inhibitor; bare Al nanoparticle fillers corrode and agglomerate. The combined effect of a cerium conversion layer and a silane graft on Al nanoparticles, before and after inclusion in epoxy, is unreported.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/need), s2 (HYP/gap), s3 (HYP/hypothesis), s4 (DES/base_system), s5 (DES/modification), s6 (DES/variable_sweep), s7 (PRC/deposition), s8 (PRC/synthesis), s9 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The treated particle surface carries CeO2, Ce2O3 and Ce-OH over aluminium oxide and metallic Al. APTES is chemically grafted through Si-O-Al with free amine ends; Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al carry the most silane.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Surface treatment slows nanoparticle corrosion in pH 1: evolved H2 falls from 1.7 mL (Al) to 0.7 mL (Si-Al-2). Coating barrier resistance after 57 d in 3.5% NaCl: S2 and S4 reach ~10^10.5 ohm cm2 against ~10^4.5 for the blank.
states.detail: Absorbed: s12 (PRP/value), s14 (PRP/value), s15 (PRP/value), s17 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Epoxide groups of the resin react with the primary amine of APTES

states.title: Performance state
states.head: After 360 h salt spray the S2 and S4 coatings corrode only along the scribe while blank and untreated-filler coatings are destroyed

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Cerium conversion plus APTES grafting protects the nanoparticle itself and, through better dispersion and bonding, the whole epoxy coating

nodes.title: XPS, F2
nodes.head: Al 2p resolves into two components at 75.4 eV (aluminium oxide) and 78.2 eV (aluminium), the metal component the larger. O 1s deconvolutes into CeO2 ~529, Ce2O3 ~530, Al-O ~531 and Ce-OH ~532 eV.

panel_conditions.condition: Al 2p high resolution spectrum of Ce-Al modified at pH 3.8

nodes.note: peak heights ~17 and ~72 counts read off the F2b ordinate judge re-read of F2c: the fitted components peak at CeO2 ~100, Ce2O3 ~285, Al-O ~380 and Ce-OH ~250 counts, so the Ce2O3 component alone exceeds Ce-OH and CeO2+Ce2O3 dominate it, against the text's statement that the cerium-oxide contribution is much less intense than the hydroxide. The figure labels the 530 eV component 'Ce2O', which is a figure typo for Ce2O3. the survey marks Ce 3d only with a dashed circle; the 820-880 eV enlargement, which sits outside the F2a crop and is only visible in the whole-figure image, is flat scatter between ~1150 and ~1280 counts with no resolvable doublet, so the Ce layer is at or below the XPS detection limit.

use: The results of high resolution analysis are given in Fig. 2b, c and Table 4.

High resolution Al 2p scan was fitted into two Gaussian–Lorentzian peaks of 75.41 and 78.17 eV associated with the presence of aluminium oxide and aluminium metal on the surface of the sample, respectively (Fig. 2b) [44–47].
The results of high resolution analysis are given in Fig. 2b, c and Table 4.
Thus, more information about the state of Ce oxide/hydroxide layer was obtained from the O1s high resolution spectrum, which is shown in Fig. 2c.
